card.name: Aati Kalenja
card.tagline: Tulu monsoon-spirit dance that wards off disease
card.profile: Aati Kalenja is a ritual folk dance of Tulu Nadu (coastal Karnataka and Kasaragod, Kerala) performed during the Tulu month of Aati (July-August), the heavy-monsoon season (Wikipedia). A performer of the Nalike (or Mugera) community masquerades as the nature-spirit Kalenja, wearing a costume of tender coconut fronds and an areca-leaf headgear (mudi), face painted, holding a palm-leaf parasol. He visits homes dancing to the tembere drum while a companion sings the paddana, sprinkling water mixed with turmeric, charcoal and tamarind to drive away disease and misfortune (Swarajya; Daijiworld).
card.insight: The tradition is endangered: modernization and reduced paddy cultivation have left it confined to a few villages, prompting a Wikimedia-supported revival of the Mugera variant in 2024 (Wikimedia Diff).
